newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian average lending rate drops to 10.8 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian average lending rate drops to 10.8 pct.

text.p: Croatia's average lending rate dropped to 10.8 percent on Tuesday from 12.2 percent amid lower demand for fresh funds.
Supply at 77 million kuna largely overshot demand but some borrowers were left empty handed as they had exceeded debt limits set by creditors, dealers said.
Of 47.4 million kuna settlements, only some 30 million were fresh borrowings. The central bank said it also had 147.6 million kuna in outstanding Lombard funds but expected some would be repaid.
Call money loans were again struck at 10.5 percent, compared with a weighted 11 percent rate on Monday.
Interbank term rates ranged between 11 percent for eight-day and 16 percent for two-month deals. Savings banks paid 18 percent for two-month kuna.
Insurers rolled over one-week money at a stable 9.0 percent.
The central bank calculated its kuna midrates for Wednesday firmer at 6.1759 against the dollar and 3.5769 versus the mark. -- Metka Jelenc, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
